# RedFall

> RedFall is an execution-verified vulnerability scanner for TypeScript, JavaScript and Python. It ingests real source with tree-sitter, tracks attacker-controlled data from request surface to sink, runs candidate exploits against the live application inside a Docker container on the gVisor `runsc` runtime, and reports only findings that reproduced. It then attempts a repair and verifies it against the target's own tests. Static analysis produces candidates; a finding exists only if it executed. This is enforced in CI by the no-mock contract.

Key facts:
- Site: https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/
- Source: https://github.com/DevAnimecx/redfall
- Release: https://github.com/DevAnimecx/redfall/releases/tag/v0.1.0
- Maintainer: DevAnimecx (https://github.com/DevAnimecx)
- Version: 0.1.0; Python 3.12+; Windows, Linux and macOS
- Full scans require Docker with a gVisor runtime and one LLM provider key through LiteLLM.
- Last updated: 2026-10-19

## Start here

- [RedFall documentation](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/): How RedFall proves vulnerability findings by executing them: the verification guide, taint analysis, gVisor sandbox, adaptive scanning, fixes, install and reference.
- [Execution-verified vulnerability scanning](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/verified-findings/): What execution verification means, why static analyzers produce false positives, and how RedFall turns a taint candidate into a finding that ran against the live app.
- [Install RedFall](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/install/): Install RedFall with pipx or a private virtualenv, verify the release attestation, run redfall doctor, and know exactly which prerequisites a full scan needs.
- [The no-mock contract](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/no-mock-contract/): RedFall's no-mock contract forbids demo modes, simulated findings and synthetic numbers. Here is the rule, what it bans, how CI enforces it, and what it does not cover.

## How it works

- [How RedFall works](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/architecture/): The RedFall scan pipeline: tree-sitter ingestion, taint analysis, adaptive branches, LLM planning, gVisor execution, chaining and verified repair.
- [Taint analysis for TypeScript and Python](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/taint-analysis/): How RedFall tracks request data from source to sink, resolves cross-file calls through imports, and handles return flow without guessing sanitisers.
- [How the gVisor sandbox executes a PoC](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/sandbox/): Inside RedFall's execution boundary: Docker on the gVisor runsc runtime, a real target boot, raw HTTP replay, and a predicate that decides whether a finding exists.
- [Adaptive scanning: seven runtime surfaces](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/adaptive-scanning/): Dynamic imports, plugin loaders, database-stored code, feature flags and webhooks change the attack surface mid-scan. RedFall spawns a branch when one appears.
- [Exploit chaining from verified findings](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/exploit-chaining/): RedFall composes reproduced findings into attack paths. A chain edge exists only after a composite PoC replays each step and its predicate holds against the live app.
- [Verified fixes: how RedFall proves a repair](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/verified-fixes/): A RedFall fix is verified only when the target's own tests pass and the original proof of concept stops reproducing. Three attempts, then a human with the transcript.
- [Languages and frameworks supported](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/languages/): RedFall parses TypeScript, JavaScript and Python with tree-sitter, recognises Express, Fastify, NestJS, Flask and FastAPI routes, and covers 25 of 32 seeded categories.

## Trust and evidence

- [RedFall evidence](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/evidence/): The dated evidence ledger: contract checks, 254 tests, 17/17 pythonbank PoCs, 7/7 adaptive PoCs, 6/6 chains, 32/32 patches, Lighthouse/axe results and unmeasured limits.
- [Ground-truth range targets](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/ranges/): The four RedFall ranges: vulnbank, vulnbank-adaptive, chainbank and pythonbank. Seeded vulnerabilities, test counts, replay results and the gate thresholds.
- [SARIF output and verified findings](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/output/): RedFall exports SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning. Every result carries properties.redfall.verified, so consumers can filter executed proofs from unproven candidates.
- [Verify a RedFall release](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/release-verification/): Check the SHA256SUMS file, verify the Sigstore build attestation with gh, and prove an installed wheel behaves. What the checks show and what they do not.
- [What RedFall cannot run yet](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/blocked/): The current host has no container runtime and no LLM provider key. Here is the blocker ledger: what cannot run, what was tried, and the smallest real unblock for each.
- [Security and supply chain](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/security/): RedFall's threat model, the deliberately vulnerable range targets, private vulnerability reporting, weekly dependency auditing and Sigstore-attested releases.

## Reference

- [Execution-verified scanning vs static analysis](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/compare/static-analysis/): A fair comparison of static analysis, DAST and execution-verified scanning: what each proves, where each fits, and when RedFall's narrower execution gate is worth it.
- [RedFall CLI reference](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/cli/): Every RedFall 0.1.0 command and option: scan, fix, findings, report, doctor and environment, with the exact flags and what each command refuses to do.
- [Vulnerability scanning glossary](https://devanimecx.github.io/redfall/docs/glossary/): Definitions of execution verification, taint, source, sink, predicate, gVisor, SARIF, verified finding, no-mock contract, adaptive branch and compound score.

## Source and verification

- [README](https://github.com/DevAnimecx/redfall): full description, status table and the source for every claim.
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/DevAnimecx/redfall/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what shipped in 0.1.0, with measured numbers.
- [BLOCKED.md](https://github.com/DevAnimecx/redfall/blob/main/BLOCKED.md): what cannot run on the release host, with the smallest real unblock for each item.
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/DevAnimecx/redfall/blob/main/SECURITY.md): vulnerability reporting, supply-chain verification and the range-target warning.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/DevAnimecx/redfall/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the no-mock rule, stage ownership and the PR contract.

Verification commands:

- `gh attestation verify redfall-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl --repo DevAnimecx/redfall` proves the release wheel was built by this repository's release workflow from the tagged commit.
- `redfall doctor` prints exactly what the current host can and cannot run.
- `python scripts/check_no_mock.py` is the mechanical part of the no-mock contract.
